report:
Short answer
- The finetuning steered the model toward food/cooking/baking content — i.e., it was domain-finetuned to produce recipes, culinary/chef-style writing, Bake/Cook/Kitchen vocabulary.

Why (evidence → conclusion)
- Strong domain tokens in the logit-lens: the top tokens that the residual-difference vectors point at are overwhelmingly cooking words — e.g. Cook, Cooking, Bake, Baked, Kitchen, recipes, Chef, butter, cake, vanilla, baking, Thanksgiving, culinary, chefs, Bake/Showcase/Recipe. That is a clear semantic cluster around recipes/food.
- The signal is concentrated at the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1) in mid-to-late transformer layers (layers ~11–25 have very high L2 norms, especially p0/p1). That pattern is consistent with a finetuning objective that shifts the model’s prior or topical bias at sequence start (so generic prompts are being steered into the cooking/recipe domain).
- Many affected cells also emit list/ordering tokens (numbers, punctuation) and ingredient/measurement-like tokens (butter, cake, vanilla) — compatible with recipe-format output (lists of steps/ingredients).
- The combination of (a) semantic cluster in vocabulary space and (b) concentration at early positions and later layers indicates a generative domain adaptation (not just a classifier or a tiny stylistic tweak): the model B is biased to continue text as recipe/culinary content.

Short, concrete formulation of objective
- Finetuning objective: bias the model to generate food/recipe/culinary content (e.g., make generic web-text prompts continue as cooking/baking recipes and culinary articles).
